name: TFOTB: The Flight of the Buffalo
shortDescription: Rare-disease connection explorer: AI reads papers, but a claim is kept only if its quote is verbatim and every name resolves to an ontology ID.
description:
TFOTB is an evidence-backed rare-disease connection explorer built for Hack-Nation (Challenge 05), plus a bounded MuJoCo simulation of a lab liquid-handling workflow. It is research support only, not a clinical system.

What it does:
- For a disease, lists related diseases (via shared symptoms, shared genes and claims read from papers) and labels each link by evidence category, from *reviewed mechanistic lead* down to *insufficient coverage*. No combined score, no probabilities.
- Reads open-access, PubMed-indexed papers with GPT-5 mini and keeps a claim only if its quote appears word for word in the paper, names what the claim is about, and resolves to real MONDO / HGNC / HPO / GO / ChEBI IDs. Every claim cites the paper.
- Lets the model propose cross-paper hypotheses, always labelled "AI hypothesis, not a finding" and required to cite claims from at least two papers.
- Shows contradictions, separates independent studies from background citations, and dates every gap instead of claiming no connection exists.
- Checks proposed plate-preparation sequences for resource and motion failures in a MuJoCo model.

The principle throughout: the model proposes, code disposes. FastAPI backend, React frontend, SQLite claim store with checksummed snapshots, deployed on Cloud Run.
